S2 policy-engine: deterministic fail-closed verdict between plan_action and resolve_action
S3 action-executor: PUBLISH via Tool Gateway, idempotency key wired, RetryPolicy unlocked

S4a DONE: run_publish submits through the Tool Gateway (no more self-built XHSClient); xhs.publish orphan disappears; cdp_endpoint joins the tool signature so per-account profiles survive the migration; account_id finally reaches the platform layer on the mainline path (closing the other half of the S2 defect)

S4b DONE (feat/p2a-s4b-publish-confirmation): publish_gate between the AI verdict and the irreversible publish; dynamic interrupt + Command(resume=...); WorkflowStatus.AWAITING_PUBLISH wired into BOTH derive_status paths; auto_publish honoured (it was declared-but-unread) so the default path is unchanged; separate publish_confirmation key (never human_feedback); default-refuse on any value that is not the literal 'confirmed'; /resume has NO default decision. Does NOT emit a PublishIntent, so open question 1 stays open -- see the revision note in prd.md.

S5a DONE (feat/p2a-s5a-credential-provisioning): services/xhs_credentials.py owns 'which account's credential, sourced from where' -- the account's own account_credentials row first, the deployment XHS_COOKIE second (declared in .env.example since day one, unread until now), nothing third; fail-closed at the reader boundary, and 'no account store' separated from 'unreadable account store'. One answer, two readers: the cookie goes to XHSClient (the read factory's docstring admitted it had none to hand over, so _require_readable fired on every call) and the scopes go to the Tool Gateway, so xhs.publish's declared auth_scope stops being decorative (every production caller passed granted_scopes=None, which the Gateway reads as UNCHECKED -- S3's own docstring said 'nothing in this repo owns a publish grant yet'). The executor gains a FOURTH pre-Gateway refusal (409, its own error code) placed FIRST because entitlement does not depend on the artifact. NOT done, deliberately: no writer for account_credentials (that is the login flow's job, recorded as a residue), no scope check on the mainline publish (its account may be '' by design, so a check there would prejudge open question 1), and no scope check on the read path (PermissionDeniedError raises, which would turn a runtime condition into a wiring exception and break the degradation branch). S5 is SPLIT: this is the authorisation half; provenance/audit/docs stay for S5b.

subtasks.title: S5c DONE (feat/p2a-s5c-contract-and-fallback): docs/publish-action-protocol.md; 501 fallback (execute_action's default arm now raises instead of answering with another capability's receipt) ; open question 1 adjudicated as a decision + trigger

notes:
S4b landed on feat/p2a-s4b-publish-confirmation (base ce9eff54). Scope: only the WAIT. A human authorisation gate (`publish_gate`) now sits between the AI quality verdict and the irreversible publish -- until this slice 'the content is good enough' and 'you may post it' were the SAME event, so an AI gate could decide on its own to perform an irreversible external action. The gate uses a DYNAMIC interrupt() (not interrupt_before) for two reasons, neither stylistic: Command(resume=...) only resumes dynamic interrupts (brief/ripple/blogger already use that channel; a static entry would need a second one just for this gate), and builder.compile() appears TWICE in build_graph() (dev/prod) so interrupt_before would put 'this gate exists' in two places while add_node writes it once -- single entry, no drift. SIX pre-existing facts had to be handled first: (1) two interrupt paradigms coexist in this repo; (2) WorkflowStatus is DERIVED, not stored, and derive_status recognises a gate through TWO independent paths (next_nodes gate name, and interrupts[0].value['gate']) -- both were extended, since adding one leaves the other silently misreporting; (3) `auto_publish` was a DECLARED-BUT-UNREAD key: POST /start and POST /api/review/submit both advertise '审核通过后自动发布', the schema/DB/state all carry it, and backend/graph/** never read it -- this slice honours it, which is precisely what keeps the change to the DEFAULT path only (without it, every existing auto-publish workflow would suddenly need a human click -- that is changing behaviour, not adding a gate); (4) `dry_run` has two sources (workflow-level state + decision-level publish_options) and its rule lived inline in PublisherAgent.execute; (5) run_publish has THREE call sites and the other two (/publish-retry, the free-publish route) are ALREADY explicit human channels, so no gate was added there; (6) 'cancelled' is not new semantics -- derive_status priority 1 and _check_terminal already map phase=CANCELLED, so refusing a publish needs NO new status value, only AWAITING_PUBLISH. KEY DESIGN: (a) publish_confirmation is a SEPARATE state key from human_feedback -- merging the two is the natural refactor and it would silently break routing, because review_outcome reads human_feedback.decision, so a gate write there would overwrite the verdict it routes on; (b) the failure direction is CLOSED: publish_gate_outcome only accepts the literal 'confirmed', everything else (missing, typo, old client) is a refusal, because a confirmation gate that reads an unrecognised value as 'go ahead' turns every version skew into an unconfirmed real publish; (c) there is deliberately NO default resume_value, unlike brief/ripple/blogger whose defaults ('skip'/'accept') continue something already authorised -- here the default would BE the irreversible act, so an empty /resume describes what to send and runs nothing; (d) a refusal sets phase=CANCELLED rather than ERROR (a human saying 'not this one' is a decision, not a fault) and rather than leaving PUBLISHING (publisher is skipped, so the run would have no next node and derive_status would report COMPLETED for a note never posted); (e) publish_is_dry_run is now ONE rule with TWO readers (PublisherAgent picks its mock path, the gate decides whether to ask), so gate and publisher cannot disagree about whether anything left the machine -- which is why auto_publish is compared with strict `is True` (no twin reader: a near-miss value means nobody really made the statement, so stay closed) while dry_run uses truthiness (its twin would also go mock, so they agree). REVISION vs the plan row: the row also promised 'PublisherAgent emits a PublishIntent and stops there' plus a ruling on open question 1. That half was NOT built -- routing the mainline through the control plane (intent -> Policy -> Executor) is an architectural migration, orthogonal to the safety property 'never publish without human authorisation' (the same split argument as S4a), and S4a had already settled on not emitting intents. So the mainline still calls run_publish directly and open question 1 (ActionIntentRequest.account_id required vs the mainline's implicit account) REMAINS UNADJUDICATED -- this slice has no code path that produces an ActionIntent, so there is nothing for the ruling to attach to. Recorded as a revision in prd.md rather than left as a plan row that looks done. GATES: pytest -q 3227 passed / 3 skipped (S4a's 3151 / 3 skipped + 76 = 36 + 9 + 10 + 4 + 1 + 14 + 2, exactly the new cases added -- nothing deleted, no existing assertion weakened); ruff check + ruff format --check clean; mypy backend --python-version 3.12 clean (203 files); P1b baseline drift within threshold; tool_runtime_gate.py OK; frontend type-check + vitest + i18n:check clean. MUTATION CHECK 22/22 killed, each applied from pristine content with a named killer, and all 16 named killers were first run on the untouched tree so no 'killed' verdict can come from an already-red test. Two notable ones: M12's FIRST run was an ANCHOR FAILURE, not a survivor (it anchored on `if terminal := _check_terminal(state)`, a shape 15 routers share) -- the recorded result is the re-run after tightening the anchor. And a probe side-product: Command(resume={}) does NOT resolve the interrupt at all -- LangGraph reads an empty payload as 'nothing to resume with', the node re-raises and the thread stays parked with an untouched state. That is the safest reading of a blank answer and it is distinguishable from a refusal, so it got its own test rather than being folded into the refusal group. TRIPWIRES: the evaluator-gate topology test pinning 'the publisher verdict edge lands on the publisher node' went red by design and was RESHAPED, not deleted (renamed, expectation moved to publish_gate, plus two new assertions for the gate's own branch); tests/integration/test_evaluator_pause_resume.py's next-node assertion moved (("publisher",) -> ("publish_gate",)) under the same discipline as S4a's orphan tripwire.

-- S4a --
S4a landed on feat/p2a-s4a-mainline-gateway (base 5a76cd8a). Scope: only the SUBMIT moved. run_publish no longer builds an XHSClient; it makes one `runtime.tools.invoke("xhs.publish", payload, thread_id=...)` call via BaseAgent.tools (shared_gateway). Ordering is deliberately untouched -- no PublishIntent, no confirmation wait -- because S4 was split: 'reach the Gateway' and 'wait for a human' are orthogonal, and merging them makes the 'migration does not change the contract' red line impossible to verify in isolation. S4b takes the wait. THREE pre-existing facts had to be handled first, found by recon: (1) the mainline never passed account_id at all -- the S2 defect ('account-keyed cooldown has no production writer') had TWO paths from the same XHSPublisher.publish_note, S3 closed the control-plane one, this closes the mainline one; (2) the tool hardcoded settings.platform.cdp_endpoint while the mainline resolves per account, so a straight migration would have silently sent every multi-account publish to the global browser profile -- cdp_endpoint is now a tool parameter (explicit wins, empty falls back to global so the control plane is unchanged); (3) BaseAgent.tools is a property returning shared_gateway(), which PublisherAgent previously bypassed entirely. KEY DESIGN: _publish_gateway_account_id is NOT _publish_account_id. The former returns "" when unspecified, the latter falls back to "default". The idempotency RECORD keeps "default" (compute_publish_id needs a stable string to hash; changing it would re-key every existing record and silently disarm the duplicate guard) while the PLATFORM layer gets "" (handing it "default" would file unattributed posts under account:default and change the meaning of a guardrail that works today). Two call sites, two requirements, two functions. _result_from_gateway is the single place Gateway vocabulary (ok/error_kind) is translated back into the publish_result contract (status/error), which is what keeps the 8 downstream consumers byte-unchanged (analyst/calibrator/analytics/free/workflow/hydration/omp_bridge). Two contract translations were ACCEPTED rather than patched: the timeout wording now belongs to the runtime ("timeout after 900s" replaces the method-name-carrying exception text; the test asserts the VERDICT -- status unknown + error_type publish_result_unknown -- not the wording), and the "RuntimeError: cookie expired..." prefix is harmless because classify_publish_error is a substring match, so auth_expired is unchanged. THE PINNED TRIPWIRE FIRED AND WAS RETARGETED, NOT DELETED: test_audit's 'the only orphan is the publisher' said in its own docstring that P2a wiring a publisher would fail it on purpose; it now asserts orphans == () as test_no_capability_is_left_without_an_agent, and the four-tool-users list became five. MOOT POINT WORTH RECORDING: the mutation 'the tool ignores the cdp_endpoint it is handed' SURVIVED on the first full run. Asking 'is the mutated code actually executed?' showed it is NOT -- every test replaces _get_publisher wholesale, so the factory body (and the explicit-beats-global rule) had ZERO execution coverage. A real gap, not a fake mutation: TestGetPublisherEndpointSelection now patches only XHSPublisher so the selection logic really runs, and the mutant dies. Gates: pytest 3151 passed/3 skipped (3144 + 7 = exactly the new cases: test_run_publish +4, test_xhs_publisher +3 -> zero existing cases changed apart from the intended tripwire), ruff 499 files, mypy 202 files clean, P1b baseline drift within threshold, tool_runtime_gate OK with publisher.py declared=1 invoked=1 and the orphan line GONE (named by agents: 10, orphans == ()). Mutation self-check 13/13 killed, each from original bytes by a named assertion; M1/M2/M12 (declaration/call-site capability names) are killed by the GATE first, which is the point of a compile-time rule. Stub seam: patch backend.tools.xhs.publisher._get_publisher -- browser layer only -- so the tool's normalisation, the catalog and the Gateway all really run; file runtime dropped 125.8s -> 4.3s, i.e. those tests used to touch a real browser. Open question 3 is now half-answered in code: the mainline passes its content-level publish_id AS the runtime's request-level idempotency_key (documented in-place, still no formal verdict). Open question 1 and the 501 fallback remain S4b/S5's.

-- S5a --
S5a landed on feat/p2a-s5a-credential-provisioning (base 2ce07e38). Scope: only the CREDENTIAL. P1c named this hole twice and left it: tools/xhs/trending.py said 'credential plumbing (which account's cookie, sourced from where) belongs to P2a', and creator_agent/execution.py said 'nothing in this repo owns a publish grant yet'. Recon found FOUR pre-existing facts. (1) The read path could not be credentialed because the factory built XHSClient with no cookie at all -- _require_readable's own docstring said 'today this guard fires on every call', i.e. the three read capabilities never read anything in production. (2) account_credentials (allow-list XHS_COOKIE/XHS_USER_ID) has NO production writer: the whole repo only creates the table, reads it, and strips SYSTEM_KEYS out of it -- the QR login writes the CDP profile, not the table, so what is missing is a writer, not a reader. (3) XHS_COOKIE/XHS_USER_ID are declared in .env.example and backend/config/settings.py had no cookie field at all -- another declared-but-unread key, same family as S4b's auto_publish. (4) auth_scope was declared AND enforced by the Gateway, but every production caller passed granted_scopes=None, which the Gateway documents as UNCHECKED -- an unchecked requirement is indistinguishable from no requirement, so xhs.publish's auth_scope had been decorative since S1. KEY DESIGN: (a) one owner, two readers -- the cookie and the scopes come off the same XhsCredential, so 'this call carried a credential' and 'its scope was granted' cannot disagree (the S4b publish_is_dry_run pattern); (b) an account's own credential is FINAL -- never overridden by the deployment default, not even when unusable, because falling through would read and publish as an identity the caller did not name; (c) a row is a statement and an unset env var is not -- an empty row is a cleared credential and stays final, while an empty XHS_COOKIE means nobody configured one, so source comes back empty rather than naming a source that supplied nothing (deliberate asymmetry, written into the module docstring); (d) fail-closed on the BOUNDARY, so any reader -- injected ones included -- that raises yields an unusable credential with NO fallback, because unknown is not permission to act as somebody else (the S2 lesson); (e) 'no account store' is separated from 'unreadable account store': is_pool_ready() false is a configuration fact (db/accounts is Postgres-only, no memory fallback), so the deployment credential still applies; (f) usability is presence AND shape (XHSCookieParser.is_valid) so a cookie with no login material cannot put the HTTP client in the 'configured but every call fails' state can_read exists to detect; (g) ONE rule grants both scopes -- the credential IS the account's identity evidence, and deriving write from 'a browser is reachable' would make the grant flip when a Chrome process stops, because reachability is not entitlement; (h) the credential refusal is the FOURTH pre-Gateway refusal and it is placed FIRST, not because it is cheapest but because entitlement does not depend on the artifact -- conditioning it on an artifact read would let an unentitled account be told its CONTENT was the problem and would make the verdict depend on the store being reachable; (i) the required scope is READ from the registry rather than restated, since a literal is a second statement of the same requirement and its drift is silent (the Gateway would still enforce the declared one while the executor refused for the other); (j) the refusal is 409, not 403 -- 403 stays reserved for the policy engine's rule, while this is 'the caller may ask and the capability is executable, but the ACCOUNT has no credential', the same family as the content refusal and with the same guarantee that the Gateway was never reached and no receipt was minted. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: no writer for account_credentials (that is credential PROVISIONING inside a 1900-line login module plus a new upsert API -- a different concern, pinned as a test and recorded as a residue: today the only source that really supplies a credential is the deployment XHS_COOKIE); no scope check on the mainline publish, because _publish_gateway_account_id deliberately returns '' when unspecified (S4a's decision) and '' resolves no grant, so a check there would prejudge open question 1; no scope check on the read path, because PermissionDeniedError RAISES by design and would turn a runtime condition into a wiring exception that blows through trend_scout's degradation branch -- a worse failure mode for the same situation. REVISION: S5 is split into S5a (authorisation, this slice) and S5b (DecisionRecord immutability + persisted refusal audit + docs/publish-action-protocol.md + the 501 fallback + the open-question rulings), because bundling them lets 'is the authorisation right' and 'is the audit complete' mask each other -- the same split argument as S4a/S4b, and the split is recorded in prd.md rather than left as a plan row that looks done. GATES: pytest -q 3255 passed / 3 skipped (S4b's 3227 + 28 = 19 + 5 + 1 + 2 + 1, exactly the new cases; no existing case deleted, two reshaped); ruff check + format --check clean at 505 files; mypy backend --python-version 3.12 clean (204 files); P1b baseline drift within threshold; tool_runtime_gate.py OK. MUTATION CHECK 17/17 killed, each from pristine bytes with a named killer, and the 23 named killers were first run on the untouched tree (step 0) so no 'killed' verdict can come from an already-red test. TRIPWIRES: the credential refusal ranking first changed the ACCOUNT PRECONDITION of the existing 'every refusal precedes the Gateway' cases, so the two advisor factories now state a credential for the account (a valid a1= cookie) -- the assertions are untouched, and 'a publish test's account must be credentialed' is the truer fixture; the old one only ran because the rule did not exist. The default-dispatcher test now supplies XHS_COOKIE and therefore exercises the whole production chain: environment -> xhs_credentials -> scopes -> xhs.publish's declaration -> Gateway -> tool. STALE DOC FIXED IN PASSING: docs/tool-runtime.md still listed 'xhs.publish has a declaration but no caller (P2a)', which S4a had already closed.

-- S5b --
S5b landed on feat/p2a-s5b-record-fidelity (base af7b8f35): DecisionRecord judgment frozen (single writer _append_feedback: feedback append-only + updated_at; both adapters route through it) + durable refusal audit (kind="action": policy_denied from the API route, publish_refused from the publish gate; ACTION_EVENT_KIND pinned against EVENT_KINDS). Chose A3 (name and enforce the mutable boundary) over A1/A2 (feedback in its own table) because no consumer depends on payload byte-stability. S5c remains: docs/publish-action-protocol.md + 501 fallback (execute_action's else -> exhaustive match with a fail-closed default) + the ticket-level ruling on pending question 1/3.

-- S5c -- (feat/p2a-s5c-contract-and-fallback, base 98cee316) The LAST P2a slice. Three things. (1) docs/publish-action-protocol.md -- the single written home of the publish action protocol: the four refusals and which layer each one lives in (plan 403 / execute unconfirmed 409 / credential 409 / not-wired 501 / content-unavailable 409), why the pre-execution check ORDER is part of the design (entitlement does not depend on the artifact, so it is refused before the content is even looked at), the two layers of idempotency (content-level compute_publish_id + request-level UNIQUE(account_id, idempotency_key)), what a refusal leaves behind, the 4 steps to add a capability, and the known residues. (2) THE 501 FALLBACK: ActionCapabilityNotWiredError (creator_agent/repository.py:98) had ZERO raisers repo-wide -- only the route's except (api/routes/creator_agent.py:474-475) consumed it -- so that 501 contract had never once executed. The root cause was not the route: CreatorAdvisor.execute_action ended its dispatch chain with a bare `else` that answered every kind other than REQUEST_MORE_EVIDENCE with ANOTHER capability's receipt. All four members are reachable today, so the arm was unreachable -- but a durable, immutable receipt that CLAIMS work that never happened is exactly what it would have produced for a fifth kind or a version-skewed row. Fixed by naming REQUEST_MORE_EVIDENCE explicitly and making the default arm raise. (3) OPEN QUESTION 1 ADJUDICATED as a DECISION with a trigger, not a TODO: there is still no caller that produces an ActionIntent (the mainline calls run_publish directly), so the decision has no landing site; the ruling is 'account_id stays explicitly required, and any future migration of the mainline onto the control plane must resolve the account explicitly and must never invent one' -- the same rule as S4a's '' rather than 'default' and S5b's 'never invent a thread'. Also: ActionCapabilityNotWiredError now takes ActionCapability | str (raw, NOT narrowed to the enum -- the raiser holds whatever the intent carried, and narrowing would make the error constructor throw a second error on the very case it exists for, turning 501 into 500) plus a kind_label property; the route reads kind_label (it previously read .action_kind.value, which would AttributeError on a raw str). Deliberate non-changes: no destructive default (the arm must refuse, never return a generic failure receipt), no enum narrowing, no new writers for account_credentials. Tests +4 (exec +3: one behavioural, one STRUCTURAL via inspect.getsource(CreatorAdvisor.execute_action) checking every declared member has its own arm -- an `is` chain cannot be introspected, so the invariant takes a behaviour + structure pair; api +1: a path test through execute_action rather than a hand-constructed error object). Gates 3283 passed / 3 skipped, ruff 506 files, mypy 204 files, baseline within threshold, tool gate OK. Mutation 8/8 killed; M6 was an EQUIVALENT MUTANT (StrEnum makes str(member) == value), so the redundant defensive spelling was DELETED rather than tested around it.
